title: VPBank Hanoi International Marathon 2026 Review: From Sword Lake to Walking Street
seo_title: VPBank Hanoi Marathon 2026 Review | Hoan Kiem Lake
meta_description: VPBank Hanoi International Marathon 2026 review: October 18, starting at Hoan Kiem Lake -- Hanoi's legendary Lake of the Returned Sword.
dek: Set for 18 October 2026, this bank-backed marathon starts at Hoan Kiem Lake -- Hanoi's legendary 'Lake of the Returned Sword' -- and finishes at Tran Nhan Tong walking street, with Early Bird registration open.
verdict: The VPBank Hanoi International Marathon starts at one of Vietnam's most storied landmarks: Hoan Kiem Lake, a freshwater lake at the historic centre of Hanoi tied to a 15th-century legend about a magical sword and a Golden Turtle. That's a genuinely evocative starting point, distinct from the mall- and stadium-anchored venues dominating most of this research batch. Backed by VPBank, a major Vietnamese bank, the race offers four distances from 5K to the full 42.195K, with Early Bird registration currently open. Finishing at Tran Nhan Tong walking street keeps the course within Hanoi's historic urban core.

sections.heading: Starting at the Lake of the Returned Sword
paragraphs: The race starts at Hoan Kiem Lake and finishes at Tran Nhan Tong walking street, offering four distances: 5K, 10K, 21.1K and the 42.195K full marathon. [1] Hoan Kiem Lake -- meaning 'Lake of the Returned Sword' -- is a 12-hectare freshwater lake at the historic centre of Hanoi, roughly 700m long and 250m wide. [2]

sections.heading: A 15th-Century Legend Behind the Name
paragraphs: The lake's name comes from a legend in which King Le Loi received a magical sword from the Dragon King to defeat Chinese invaders; after his victory, a Golden Turtle surfaced while he was boating on the lake and requested the sword back, which he returned -- giving the lake its name. [2] The lake is now surrounded by the Ngoc Son Temple complex, The Huc Bridge, and Turtle Tower, landmarks that give this marathon's starting point genuine cultural and legendary weight beyond a typical urban plaza.

sections.heading: Bank-Backed With Early Bird Pricing
paragraphs: VPBank, one of Vietnam's major private banks, backs the race with Early Bird pricing currently available: VND 999,000 for the 42K, 899,000 for the 21K, 699,000 for the 10K, and 599,000 for the 5K. [1] That kind of institutional financial backing suggests a well-resourced production, similar to the Techcombank Hanoi Marathon covered elsewhere in this research.

sections.heading: Two Hanoi Marathons to Distinguish
paragraphs: Notably, this is a separate event from the Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon (5th edition) covered elsewhere in this batch -- both are bank-backed Hanoi marathons but with different sponsors, start points and dates. Runners researching Hanoi marathons should confirm which specific race and sponsor they're registering for.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If starting a marathon at one of Vietnam's most legendarily significant landmarks appeals, the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon on 18 October 2026 offers genuine cultural weight alongside solid bank-backed production. Early Bird registration is open now -- worth locking in before standard pricing kicks in.
